label: Concrete/abstract classification: Classification B supplies concrete and abstract predicates on…
definition: Classification B supplies concrete and abstract predicates on the candidate domain together with required disjointness (∀ x, abstract x → ¬ concrete x). It does not require exhaustiveness, since rival criteria need not be exhaustive; for the adopted esse sense both disjointness and exhaustiveness are derived (DEF-ABSTRACT-NO-ESSE-IN-RE). Concreteness is world-independent; concreteness at a world (ConcreteAt) is existence there together with concreteness.
note: Shared typed vocabulary for #1103, replacing ad-hoc free concrete parameters where the meaning coincides. The adopted sense is DEF-CONCRETE-ESSE-IN-RE; rival criteria are sibling senses under DISAMB-CONCRETE-ABSTRACT-CRITERIA. Owner decision on #1103 (2026-11-06): https://github.com/moritzbrantner/truth-core/issues/1103#issuecomment-6683616439. See docs/notes/concrete-abstract.md. Same-dictionary packaging (#1111): DefinitionDictionaryConnections.connections relates the required disjoint proof field to AbstractConcreteDisjoint over exactly c.abstract/c.concrete, or conversely packages supplied predicates with that proof. The projection cannot define the proposition that the constructor requires; the predicate and structure therefore retain distinct typed APIs, not competing classification policies.
